prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project manages its Long Term Support (LTS) releases through a clearly defined lifecycle schedule. Based on the official Node.js Release documentation, an LTS release goes through distinct phases. The "Active" phase lasts for 18 months, followed by a "Maintenance" phase that lasts for 12 months. 

Here are the exact citations from the official documentation:

SOURCE: https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases | QUOTE: "LTS scheduling is based on the concept of Active and Maintenance phases. Every Major LTS release enters Active for 18 months, then Maintenance for 12 months." | CLAIM: Active LTS lasts for 18 months and Maintenance LTS lasts for 12 months.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release | QUOTE: "After the first 6 months, the LTS release enters the Active phase and all applicable lands on the LTS release in addition to the Current release. This phase lasts for 18 months." | CLAIM: The Active LTS phase has a duration of 18 months.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release | QUOTE: "After 18 months, the LTS release enters the Maintenance phase where only critical bug fixes and security updates are landed. This phase lasts for 12 months." | CLAIM: The Maintenance LTS phase has a duration of 12 months.
